title: Intangible assets
trigger: A newly recorded software/license cost needs support and the year's amortization is being tested.
preparer: Inspect rights and selected additions/disposals, distinguish the nature of expenditure and recalculate the supported amortization.
reviewer: Challenge rights, the recognition/capitalization basis, useful life and unsupported classifications; arithmetic is only part of the work.
limit: No automatic recognition decision from a cost label or a successful amortization calculation.
example: 120 cost / 3 years = 40 annual charge under a selected straight-line full-year profile. Rights and capitalization evidence are a separate prerequisite.

title: Property, plant and equipment
trigger: The asset register contains an addition, a disposal and changed depreciation for selected items.
preparer: Trace selected movements to support, inspect relevant assets, recalculate supported depreciation and record impairment/lease matters needing separate evaluation.
reviewer: Challenge existence/rights, repair-versus-capital classification, timing, life/residual assumptions and the treatment of disposed assets.
limit: A disposal/fully-depreciated flag is a candidate; impairment and lease conclusions require their actual supported work.

source.title: Audit program — property, plant and equipment

example: Cost 120, residual 20, life 5 gives annual straight-line charge 20 before any approved proration.

title: Investments
trigger: An investment movement or changed ownership arrangement requires classification, valuation and disclosure work.
preparer: Inspect the actual rights/arrangement and selected transactions, reconcile holdings and evaluate the applicable measurement/consolidation treatment.
reviewer: Challenge whether evidence supports control, influence or joint control and the chosen accounting basis; request specialist/component work when needed.
limit: Do not hard-code the source form's percentage shortcuts or its joint-arrangement wording as accounting conclusions.
example: Opening 10 units + acquired 5 - disposed 2 = 13; custody confirms 12, leaving one unit to investigate.

title: Inventory values and movements
trigger: Inventory movement/cost records disagree with the recorded value, or slow/damaged items need evaluation.
preparer: Reconcile quantities and values, inspect selected receipts/issues and cut-off, recalculate the supported cost profile and assess lower-value/write-down indicators.
reviewer: Challenge count-to-record coverage, ownership, method, units and the evidence for estimated realizable amounts.
limit: Attendance itself is P09-UC05. Aging or a computed shortfall alone does not decide an inventory write-down.
example: Opening 100 + receipts 20 - issues 10 + signed adjustment -3 = 107; physical 106 differs by -1.

title: Trade receivables
trigger: Selected customer balances need evidence of existence, timing and recoverability.
preparer: Trace selected balances/transactions, evaluate confirmations when used, inspect subsequent receipts and record relevant cut-off/allowance implications.
reviewer: Challenge whether subsequent cash relates to the selected debt and whether existence evidence also supports recovery; keep those assertions distinct.
limit: A nonresponse is not agreement. An aging calculation is not an automatic allowance conclusion.
example: Invoice 100 less validated subsequent receipt 60 leaves 40 before credit/allowance analysis.

title: Other long-term receivables
trigger: A long-dated balance includes principal and interest that need support and appropriate classification.
preparer: Inspect selected rights and terms, reconcile movements, recalculate supported principal/interest and assess classification and recovery evidence.
reviewer: Challenge timing, contract interpretation, valuation and whether apparent repayment actually settles the selected receivable.
limit: Complex measurement remains manual/specialist work where the selected automation does not support it.
example: Contractual 100 due after the next operating-cycle/current classification boundary needs explicit framework/contract analysis.

title: Other receivables and prepayments
trigger: A prepayment remains open after goods/services should have been received.
preparer: Inspect selected advances and their later application, recalculate period allocation under the supported basis and assess the remaining balance.
reviewer: Challenge whether receipt/use supports release to the appropriate asset/expense and whether unsupported balances need further work.
limit: A paid invoice does not alone establish that a prepayment was consumed in this period.

source.title: Audit program — other receivables and prepayments

example: A synthetic 120 prepayment over 12 equal months, with four months expired, leaves 80 unexpired under that profile.

title: Cash and cash equivalents
trigger: A bank/cash balance differs from a reconciliation or needs rights/restriction evidence.
preparer: Inspect selected receipts/payments and reconciling items, tie the relevant records and evaluate count/confirmation support and classification.
reviewer: Challenge outstanding reconciling items, authority/ownership/restrictions, timing and source authenticity.
limit: The system records actual count/confirmation work; importing a bank statement does not automatically confirm every bank relationship.

source.title: Audit program — cash and cash equivalents

example: Bank 100 versus ledger 90 with a supported +10 book-side reconciliation produces zero residual; preserve that signed taxonomy.

title: Borrowings
trigger: The recorded loan balance and interest must be tested against the actual agreement and movements.
preparer: Reconcile principal/interest movements, inspect selected support and recalculate the permitted interest profile; record condition and disclosure implications.
reviewer: Challenge contract terms, classification, covenants, collateral/guarantees and unsupported measurement assumptions.
limit: A simple interest calculation does not implement every effective-interest, modification or guarantee treatment.
example: Principal 1000 x 12% x 30/360 = interest 10 for a supported simple-segment profile.

title: Purchases and trade payables
trigger: An invoice, goods receipt and payment do not align, or a later payment may relate to an unrecorded liability.
preparer: Trace selected purchase/payable items in the relevant direction, inspect cut-off and subsequent settlement, investigate matching differences and confirmations when used.
reviewer: Challenge completeness, timing, returned goods and the actual supplier obligation; distinguish a match defect from an accounting error.
limit: Repeated document headers and one-to-many lines need the actual grain; no automatic exposure multiplication.
example: Receipt 100, supplier bill 100 and payment 110 leaves excess 10 for investigation, not an automatic loss conclusion.

title: Other payables and accruals
trigger: A period-end liability relies on an estimate or a service not yet invoiced.
preparer: Inspect selected obligations, completeness and timing, recalculate the supported accrual and compare later support with the period-end basis.
reviewer: Challenge obligation, period, method and omitted amounts; use the estimate case where judgment is significant.
limit: A later invoice amount is not automatically the correct earlier accrual without its service/period basis.

source.title: Audit program — other payables and accruals

example: A supported 40 invoice received after year end for pre-year-end goods suggests a 40 completeness test item, subject to actual obligation/support.

title: Deferred income
trigger: Cash has been received but part of the promised goods/services may remain unperformed.
preparer: Inspect the actual obligations and performance evidence, reconcile movements and evaluate/recalculate the supported release to revenue.
reviewer: Challenge whether the conditions for recognition occurred and whether the contract liability/classification remains appropriate.
limit: Invoice/payment date alone does not determine revenue recognition; no automatic all-contract accounting engine is implied.
example: Cash 120 for a uniform twelve-month service; three months earned implies revenue 30 and deferred 90 under the selected pattern.

title: Intercompany transactions
trigger: Two related entities report different reciprocal balances or a material transaction needs support.
preparer: Inspect selected terms and transactions, reconcile reciprocal amounts and evaluate related-party disclosures; route group elimination work where applicable.
reviewer: Challenge the relationship basis, unexplained differences and any asserted market/arm's-length terms.
limit: A shared identifier is a lead, not proof of control. Intercompany reconciliation does not by itself perform a group audit.
example: Entity A receivable 50 versus entity B payable 45 leaves difference 5; preserve currency/date/counterparty mapping.

title: Tax balances and expense
trigger: Tax return figures and the ledger differ, or a recalculation needs the correct period's rules.
preparer: Reconcile returns to records, inspect relevant bases and recalculate only the supported tax profile; document remaining timing/recognition issues.
reviewer: Challenge period/entity applicability, adjustments and current/deferred tax distinctions; obtain specialist advice where needed.
limit: Illustrative tax rates are not Mongolian law. A tax tie-out does not establish compliance with every tax rule.
example: Synthetic tax base 100 at an approved example rate 10% = 10; filed 9 leaves discrepancy 1.

title: Capital, reserves and dividends
trigger: A share movement or dividend affects the equity roll-forward and disclosures.
preparer: Inspect selected authorized movements, reconcile the roll-forward, recalculate supported share/dividend figures and evaluate classification/disclosure.
reviewer: Challenge actual rights/authorization, timing and capital-versus-income treatment; assess EPS only where applicable.
limit: A resolution is evidence to evaluate, not a software permission or universal EPS requirement.

source.title: Audit program — share capital, reserves and dividends

example: Opening equity 100 + profit 20 + contributions 10 - distributions 5 = closing 125; each authorization remains evidenced.

title: Revenue
trigger: A selected sale near year-end has delivery/service facts that differ from invoice or posting dates.
preparer: Inspect the selected transaction and its supporting performance/terms, recalculate supported amounts and assess timing/classification.
reviewer: Challenge the recognition basis and evidence of performance, unusual terms and subsequent reversals; do not infer success from cash alone.
limit: Cut-off flags identify candidates; software does not automatically select the applicable recognition conclusion.
example: Invoice 100 dated before year end but delivery in January is a cut-off investigation item; actual transfer terms decide treatment.

title: Cost of sales
trigger: Recorded cost of sales is inconsistent with relevant inventory movements or selected source costs.
preparer: Reconcile the selected cost/movement basis, recalculate the supported costing profile and inspect classification/cut-off.
reviewer: Challenge units, completeness, costing assumptions and whether costs relate to the relevant period's activity.
limit: The source programme repeats inventory procedures; tailor them rather than assuming the same work proves every assertion.
example: 100 units at 10 plus 100 at 20 gives periodic weighted average 15; 50 sold gives cost 750 and 150 remaining gives 2250.

title: Payroll and employee benefits
trigger: Selected payroll amounts differ from contracts, attendance, deductions or actual payment.
preparer: Trace selected people and periods, reconcile gross-to-net/payment and recalculate supported deductions/benefits; investigate exceptions.
reviewer: Challenge the actual employment/service basis, payment allocation and applicable rules; sensitive personal data need restricted access.
limit: A repeated bank account or unusual payment is a candidate, not proof of a ghost employee or fraud.

source.title: Audit program — payroll and employee benefits

example: Synthetic gross 100 less employee contribution 10 and withholding 9 gives net 81; employer contribution 5 is separate.

title: Selling and operating expenses
trigger: A selected expense may belong to another period or lack support for its nature.
preparer: Inspect selected costs, recalculate supported amounts and allocation, and assess occurrence, classification and cut-off.
reviewer: Challenge the business purpose and service period and corroborate unusual changes; route capital items for proper assessment.
limit: A management explanation or payment alone does not establish the full audit conclusion.

source.title: Audit procedures — selling and operating expenses

example: Approved service/support 30 versus recorded operating expense 35 gives a 5 investigation difference for the actual assertion.

title: Other income-statement or comprehensive-income items
trigger: A revaluation or foreign-exchange-related item needs support for its nature and presentation.
preparer: Identify the actual item, test selected underlying calculations and evaluate whether its classification/presentation follows the applicable framework.
reviewer: Challenge the item's nature and linkage rather than accepting the source form's broad account labels.
limit: Do not classify every exchange difference or revaluation automatically as OCI; framework-specific professional evaluation remains required.
example: Foreign amount 100 x accepted exact-date rate 2 = 200; recorded 190 differs by 10 in functional currency.

title: Finance costs
trigger: Interest/fees or a financing-related cost needs recalculation and classification.
preparer: Recalculate the supported profile, inspect relevant fees and timing, and evaluate expense/capitalization and disclosure treatment.
reviewer: Challenge effective-interest/lease assumptions and the actual capitalization basis; extend work where simple arithmetic is insufficient.
limit: No universal straight-line, simple-interest or capitalization rule is inferred from a successful calculation.
example: Two period-end fixed payments of 100 at zero rate give liability 200. Separately, simple loan interest follows the approved day basis.

title: Other income and expenses
trigger: A one-off grant, penalty, fee or other transaction needs an appropriate accounting basis.
preparer: Inspect selected support and conditions, recalculate supported amounts and evaluate recognition, classification and cut-off.
reviewer: Challenge the actual legal/business substance and restrictions and whether unusual items are fully explained.
limit: A transaction description or recurring ledger account is not a sufficient recognition/classification conclusion.

source.title: Audit program — other income and expenses

example: Disposal proceeds 30 less supported carrying amount 20 gives gain 10; recorded gain 8 leaves difference 2.
